newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rand Mines delays winding up order.
newsitem.headline: Rand Mines delays winding up order.

text.p: South African cash shell Rand Mines Ltd said on Tuesday that it was postponing its winding up during the three months its shares are suspended on the London and Johannesburg bourses.
The company had intended to wind itself up during the period and then distribute its cash reserves of about 30 cents a share to shareholders.
The firm has no assets and had decided on the move after an offer to inject assets into the firm was withdrawn earlier this year.

However, the firm said it had received a letter from a shareholder of 11 percent of the firm opposing the winding up and stating that there were intersted parties in putting assets back into the former mining holding company.

"Consequently the directors have decided to postpone taking steps which could result in a winding up duing the three month suspension period...this postponement will allow interested parties the opportunity of submitting a formal offer for a suitable transaction," the firm said.
It added that if no such offers were received its listing would be terminated at the end of the suspension period and the company would be wound up.
